title: A left lateral device / Know what it cannot pace

blocks.text: A left lateral device / Know what it cannot pace

AMaC MRCP PACES · R5-111 · Physical examination · PACES Station 3, cardiovascular · Skills A, B, D, E, G · 10 minutes (up to 6 examination, at least 4 questions) · Guideline dates and links in section 15 · Related AMaC: condition may appear elsewhere in a different context.
An adult followed up for inherited cardiomyopathy has a device over the left lateral chest. Examine the cardiovascular system and explain the likely device and its implications.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text:
HOOK — A lateral generator with a parasternal electrode suggests an S-ICD, which treats ventricular arrhythmia but has no sustained bradycardia or CRT pacing.
EXAMINER TRAP — Do not assume the presence of a defibrillator means that pacing support is available.

RELEASED FINDINGS — on inspection, pulse, precordial palpation and auscultation as appropriate: Healed left lateral generator scar, parasternal lead-track scar, no infraclavicular pacemaker scar, regular pulse, normal heart sounds, no congestion.
Question 1 [R4] — What is an S-ICD? | Extravascular defibrillator designed for ventricular tachyarrhythmia shocks.
Question 2 [R5] — Why choose it? | Useful when no need for ongoing pacing and transvenous leads are undesirable.
Question 3 [R6] — What after a shock? | Safety assessment, device interrogation, driving guidance specific to cause.
Question 4 [R7] — Who else needs assessment? | Relatives when inherited cardiomyopathy confirmed.
Curveball — If a candidate asks for definitive proof from examination alone: “Explain what examination suggests and which confirmatory tests you need.”

A lateral generator with a parasternal electrode suggests an S-ICD, which treats ventricular arrhythmia but has no sustained bradycardia or CRT pacing. Do not assume the presence of a defibrillator means that pacing support is available. Extravascular defibrillator designed for ventricular tachyarrhythmia shocks. Useful when no need for ongoing pacing and transvenous leads are undesirable. Safety assessment, device interrogation, driving guidance specific to cause.
